title: Connect return payload
description: The payload of a connect return, the exact JSON bytes the adapter signed. Its members come in no set order: the return carries the exact bytes signed, and the control plane parses those bytes. A connect return is the payload in base64url without padding, a dot, and the signature in base64url without padding, at most 1024 characters with no white space; the signature is 64 bytes of Ed25519 under the adapter's enrolled access key over qory-connect-return-ed25519-v1, a line feed and the payload bytes. The domain line keeps the signature from verifying as a request's signature or as a connect pass's. The adapter mints a return only after it has verified a connect pass (connect-pass.schema.json), its signature under a server key the adapter pinned and its adapter_id, so connection_id and nonce are the ones the control plane signed, and, before the pass's expires_at, only for its first arrival: a second arrival before its expires_at is refused on the adapter's page and gets no return. After expires_at, any arrival of the pass is refused pass_expired, since the adapter checks expires_at before it checks whether the nonce was seen (connect-pass.schema.json). It sends the person's browser back with a 303 to the control plane's /integrations/{connection_id}?return=<the return>, with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. The adapter sends the browser to the control plane origin it enrolled with, never to one taken from the request, a parameter or the pass. The return carries no id or name from the source. Before it changes anything, the control plane checks: the signature, under that adapter's live access key; that connection_id equals the one in the URL, and names a connection of that adapter that is pending or live; that nonce equals the nonce of the latest connect pass for that connection and the nonce bound to the person's session; that expires_at has not passed on its clock, and that no return with this nonce was accepted before, since a return is single-use; and that the signed-in person is the one who started connecting. linked makes the connection, if it is pending (connection_id in definitions.schema.json), and lets the control plane accept the adapter's grant report whose pass_nonce is this nonce. The return contains no id of the external account, so a linked return adds no grant itself: the grant of one external account is added to the connection, or replaces that account's grant, when the control plane accepts that report (grant.schema.json). refused and cancelled leave the connection as it was, pending or live, and change nothing on the control plane; the pass they answer is spent (connect-pass.schema.json). The grant of an external account that is already linked to another live connection is refused, outcome refused with the reason grant_taken, since a grant is linked to at most one live connection (connect-pass.schema.json). What the person sees when a check fails is the control plane's page, not this contract.

connection_id.description: The connection the person was making, or the live connection the person added a grant to, as the connect pass named it.

nonce.description: The nonce of the connect pass the adapter verified, as the pass carried it.

outcome.description: linked, the grant was finished in the browser that brought the pass, under that pass, and the adapter linked it, as the source confirmed it, to connection_id; refused, the adapter linked nothing, for reason; cancelled, the person stopped at the source, and the adapter linked nothing.

reason.description: Why the adapter refused, present only when outcome is refused: person_not_permitted, the person does not administer the account the grant belongs to at the source; grant_taken, the grant is already linked to another live connection, including one the adapter has just found live by listing it before replacing its pending link (definitions.schema.json); grant_not_confirmed, the source did not confirm the grant for this flow; grant_suspended, the source has suspended the grant; permission_missing, the grant lacks a permission the adapter needs; pass_expired, the pass reached the adapter after its expires_at, or more than 15 minutes ahead of it; source_unavailable, the adapter could not complete the link now, because the source or the control plane did not answer or was busy; the person may try again.

expires_at.description: When the return expires, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds, at most 300 seconds after the adapter made it. The control plane refuses a return whose expires_at has passed on its clock.
